title: 送僧归日本
title_en: Seeing a Monk Off Home to Japan
author: 钱起

glosses.zh: 上国：日本人对唐朝的尊称，指中国。
glosses.en: shàng guó: the great land, a respectful name for Tang China.

glosses.zh: 随缘：佛家的话，顺着机缘，不强求。
glosses.en: suí yuán: a Buddhist phrase, to go along with whatever chance brings.
lái tú: the journey here to China.

glosses.zh: 若梦行：像在梦里走路一样，形容路远又渺茫。
glosses.en: ruò mèng xíng: like walking in a dream, so far and unreal was the trip.

glosses.zh: 浮天：海水连着天，好像天浮在海上。
glosses.en: fú tiān: sea and sky meet, as if the sky floats on the water.
cāng hǎi: the vast blue-green sea.

glosses.zh: 去世：离开这个世界，这里指离开中国。
glosses.en: qù shì: to leave this world, here meaning to leave China.

glosses.zh: 法舟：载着佛法的船，指僧人坐的船。
glosses.en: fǎ zhōu: the boat of the Buddhist teaching, meaning the monk's boat.
shuǐ yuè: the moon reflected in the water.
chán guān: sitting in Buddhist meditation and looking deeply with a calm mind.

glosses.zh: 鱼龙：海里的鱼和龙，泛指水中的生灵。
glosses.en: yú lóng: fish and dragons, all the creatures of the sea.
fàn shēng: the sound of chanting Buddhist scriptures.
wéi lián: to love only, to treasure.

glosses.zh: 一灯影：一盏灯的光。佛家常用灯比喻佛法，能照亮人心。
glosses.en: yī dēng yǐng: the light of one lamp. Buddhists often compare their teaching to a lamp that lights up the heart.

translation.zh: 你随着机缘来到中国住下，
translation.en: Following chance, you came to stay in the great land;

translation.zh: 来时的路像在梦中走过。
translation.en: your journey here was like walking in a dream.
The sea stretches far, with the sky floating on it;

translation.zh: 你离开这里，载着佛法的船轻轻远去。
translation.en: now you leave, and your boat of the teaching sails off lightly.

translation.zh: 海上的月影和你的禅心相通，
translation.en: The moon in the water joins with your calm meditation;

translation.zh: 海里的鱼龙也来听你念经。
translation.en: the fish and dragons of the sea listen to your chanting.

translation.zh: 我最爱你船上那一盏灯光，
translation.en: Most of all I love the light of your single lamp:

translation.zh: 即使远隔万里，在我眼里也依然明亮。
translation.en: even ten thousand miles away it shines bright in my eyes.

background.zh: 唐朝时，日本常常派使者和僧人来中国学习佛法和文化。这首诗是钱起送一位日本僧人回国时写的。这位僧人叫什么名字，已经不清楚了。从中国到日本要渡过大海，在当时非常危险，所以诗人特别牵挂他。写作的具体时间也不清楚。
background.en: In the Tang dynasty, Japan often sent envoys and monks to China to study Buddhism and Chinese culture. Qian Qi wrote this poem to see off a Japanese monk going home. We no longer know the monk's name. Going from China to Japan meant crossing the open sea, which was very dangerous then, so the poet worried about him. We do not know exactly when the poem was written.

author_note.zh: 钱起，唐代中期诗人，生卒年说法不一。他是“大历十才子”之一，“大历”是唐代宗的年号。他的诗清新秀丽，名句“曲终人不见，江上数峰青”流传很广。
author_note.en: Qian Qi was a Tang poet of the middle period; sources disagree on his dates. He was one of the "Ten Talents of the Dali Era", Dali being a reign name of Emperor Daizong. His poems are fresh and graceful. His lines "The song ends and no one is in sight; on the river, a few peaks stand green" are widely known.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗处处带着佛家的味道。开头说僧人“随缘”来中国，来时像做梦，说得轻轻的，好像一切都是自然而然。接着写回去的路：大海连天，非常遥远，可他的船却“轻”，因为他心里平静，带着佛法，什么都不怕。中间两句很美：月亮映在海水里，和他的禅心一样清澈；连海里的鱼龙都来听他念经。最后诗人说，他最爱船上的那一盏灯，就算远隔万里，也一直亮在他眼里。这盏灯是船上的灯，也像是佛法的光，更像两人之间的友情。
appreciation.en: The whole poem has a Buddhist feel. It begins by saying the monk came to China "following chance", and that his journey was like a dream. It is said gently, as if everything simply happened. Then comes the way home: the sea meets the sky and is very far, yet his boat is "light", because his heart is calm and he carries the teaching, so he fears nothing. The middle lines are lovely. The moon shines in the sea, as clear as his meditating mind, and even the fish and dragons come to hear him chant. At the end the poet says he loves the lamp on the boat most of all: even ten thousand miles away, it stays bright in his eyes. It is the boat's lamp, it is like the light of the teaching, and it is also the friendship between the two men.
